items.labelEn: Load latency on L1D hit, Arm Neoverse N2 (LDR register offset)
items.labelFr: Latence de chargement sur succès L1D, Arm Neoverse N2 (LDR, décalage registre)
items.conditions: Arm Neoverse N2 (r0p0-r0p2), AArch64 integer loads (LDR/LDRB/LDUR, immediate or register offset); latency assumes an L1 data cache hit and is the maximum latency to load all destination registers.
items.locator: §3.10 Load instructions, Table 3-13 "AArch64 Load instructions", PDF p. 28
items.quote: Load register, register offset, LDR, LDRB, 4 3 L -
items.confidenceNotes: Quote condensed from table columns (whitespace collapsed). Execution latency of the instruction on an L1 hit, i.e. load-to-use; the guide gives no L2/SLC latency.

items.labelEn: Load latency on L1D hit, Arm Neoverse V3 (LDUR)
items.labelFr: Latence de chargement sur succès L1D, Arm Neoverse V3 (LDUR)
items.conditions: Arm Neoverse V3 (r0p2), AArch64 integer loads with immediate offset (LDUR/LDR); L1 data cache hit assumed; literal-pool LDR is 5 cycles in the same table.
items.locator: §3.8 Load instructions, Table 3-7 "AArch64 Load instructions", PDF p. 18
items.quote: Load register, unscaled immed LDUR, LDURB, 4 3 L -
items.confidenceNotes: Quote condensed from table columns. No L2 latency in this guide.

items.labelEn: L1 cache hit latency, Arm Cortex-A520
items.labelFr: Latence d’un succès en cache L1, Arm Cortex-A520
items.conditions: Arm Cortex-A520 (r0p1); 2 cycles best case, 4 cycles normal case (value = normal case).
items.locator: §4.11 Cache access latencies, Table 4-1 "Cortex-A520 cache access latencies", PDF p. 77
items.quote: L1 cache hit 2-4 cycles (2 is best case, 4 is normal case)
items.confidenceNotes: Quote with whitespace collapsed. In-order little core; not comparable to big cores.

items.labelEn: L2 cache hit latency, Arm Cortex-A520
items.labelFr: Latence d’un succès en cache L2, Arm Cortex-A520
items.conditions: Arm Cortex-A520 (r0p1); 10 cycles best case, 11-12 cycles normal case; value 11 = lower end of the normal case.
items.locator: §4.11 Cache access latencies, Table 4-1, PDF p. 77
items.quote: L2 cache hit 10-12 cycles (10 is best case, 11-12 is normal
items.confidenceNotes: Central value 11 chosen by the extractor inside the stated 11-12 normal range; low/high carry the full 10-12 range. L2 configuration (size, shared or not) not stated in the table.

items.labelEn: Constant cost of KPTI per kernel entry and exit (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.labelFr: Surcoût constant de KPTI par entrée et sortie du noyau (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.conditions: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 (Haswell), Linux after 4.14 with KPTI (Meltdown mitigation), with or without PCID; lower bound of the constant cost, "on the order of 400-500 cycles"; dominated by two CR3 writes (~200 cycles each per the paper).
items.protocol: LEBench microbenchmarks, each measurement repeated 10,000 times, value selected with the K-best method (K=5, 5% tolerance); HP DL160 G9, Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 2.40 GHz (Haswell), 128 GB DDR4-1866; Ubuntu Linux kernels 3.0-4.20. KPTI constant cost: empty system call with and without the KPTI patch, minus the extra cycles spent in the TLB miss handler (footnote 1).
items.locator: §4.1.1 "Remove Kernel Mappings in Userspace", p. 7, and footnote 1
items.quote: With KPTI, the lower-bound of the constant cost is on the order of 400–500 cycles
items.confidenceNotes: Value = lower end of a stated range; n per test given (10,000), dispersion not reported.

items.labelEn: Kernel entry and exit overhead without KPTI (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.labelFr: Coût d’entrée et de sortie du noyau sans KPTI (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.conditions: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3, Linux without the KPTI patch; upper bound ("less than 100 cycles").

items.labelEn: Latency of the shortest read() test without KPTI (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.labelFr: Latence du plus court test read() sans KPTI (Xeon E5-2630 v3)
items.conditions: LEBench read test, smallest size (one 4 kB page, page cache warmed), Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3, Linux 4.14-era kernel without KPTI (baseline); KPTI adds 113% without PCID, 47% with PCID.
items.protocol: LEBench microbenchmarks, each measurement repeated 10,000 times, value selected with the K-best method (K=5, 5% tolerance); HP DL160 G9, Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 2.40 GHz (Haswell), 128 GB DDR4-1866; Ubuntu Linux kernels 3.0-4.20. KPTI constant cost: empty system call with and without the KPTI patch, minus the extra cycles spent in the TLB miss handler (footnote 1).
items.locator: §4.1.1 and Figure 3 discussion, p. 7
items.quote: For the shortest read test with a baseline latency of 344ns, the PCID optimization reduces the slowdown from 113% to 47%
items.confidenceNotes: Exact kernel version of the baseline not stated in the sentence; "shortest read test" assumed to be the one-page read described in Table 2 (inference).
